behavior_class_name: Backdoor Persistence Service Foothold Behavior Class
description: Creates persistence by registering a scheduled task via the Task Scheduler 2.0 COM API that executes on a recurring time interval. The task runs under the SYSTEM account and executes a marker payload every 1 minute, confirming persistence through repeated execution logs.

persistence_installer.role: initializes COM, connects to Task Scheduler, defines a time-triggered task with repetition interval, and registers it under SYSTEM context

marker_payload.role: benign executable launched periodically by the scheduler to log execution and confirm persistence behavior

registry: scheduled task registered in Task Scheduler subsystem
process: multiple instances or repeated executions may be observed
file_system: log file grows over time with repeated entries
host: Task Scheduler Operational logs may record repeated task execution
task visible in Task Scheduler GUI
Sysmon Event ID 1 may capture repeated process execution
network: no HTTP or HTTPS traffic is required
no TCP command channel is opened

code_placement: COM-based task creation and scheduling logic are implemented in the installer. Periodic logging behavior is implemented in the marker payload.
execution_trigger: The installer executes manually. The persistence payload executes automatically every minute based on the configured time trigger.
execution_target: Task Scheduler time-based trigger subsystem and marker executable at C:\Users\Public\A06_3c_SampleApp.exe
semantic_meaning: Demonstrates time-based persistence using Task Scheduler COM API, where execution is decoupled from user interaction and occurs at regular intervals, a common technique for maintaining periodic command execution or beaconing behavior.

mitre_attack_mapping.note: Time-based recurring scheduled task persistence using Task Scheduler COM API.

control_notes.payload_effect: writes recurring log entries confirming scheduled execution

success_conditions: installer successfully initializes COM and connects to Task Scheduler
existing task A06_3c_RecurTask is removed if present
time trigger is configured with 1-minute repetition interval
task is registered under SYSTEM context
Task Scheduler activates the trigger after initial delay
payload continues writing log entries periodically
log file grows over time with repeated execution entries
no network activity or secondary payload execution occurs
